Overlap

User guide · Version 0.4.0 · Offline reference

Add lag, swing, and settling to animated controls, then bake an editable result.

Quick start · Settings · Suggested numbers · About & licence

Getting started

  1. Animate the driver or parent first. Overlap adds secondary motion to existing movement.
  2. Select the controls to simulate. Click Load selected, then check their order from root to tip.
  3. Choose Rotation or Translation and the local X/Y/Z channels you want affected.
  4. Set a frame range long enough to include the settling after the driver stops.
  5. Use Auto: continue chain for a chain endpoint. Create a locator if you want to adjust the final segment.
  6. Click Refresh source + preview. Locators show the simulation; the original rig is driven after baking.
  7. Tune the spring, then click Update preview from cached source. Refresh source after changing source keys or endpoints.
  8. Optionally enable Optimize bake, then click Bake to new animation layer.
  9. Mute the new layer to compare. To replace it, choose it in Bake layer, click Delete bake, refresh source, and bake again.

For a replacement pass, mute or delete earlier output layers before sampling source. Leaving a layer active intentionally includes its animation in the next simulation.

Controls and setup

Controls to simulate

Load the rig controls you want to add overlap to. For a chain, put the top control first and the bottom control last. Animate the driver or parent first: a chain at rest needs source movement to create a swing.

Load selected

Select controls in Maya, then click this to put them in the list. Selected parents are placed before their children. Loading a new selection clears this session's preview and endpoint; baked animation layers remain.

Up

Move the highlighted list entry one place earlier. Use this to arrange the chain from its root toward its tip. This changes the simulation order, not the rig hierarchy.

Down

Move the highlighted list entry one place later. Parent controls must appear before their selected children. The last control uses the endpoint to define its final segment.

Mode

Rotation adds swing by turning the controls, useful for tails, ears, and pendulums. Translation adds lag to their positions, useful for floating props or controls that should follow a moving target.

Apply overlap to

Choose which local control channels receive overlap. For a pendulum that bends around its local X axis, select Rotate X only. Unchecked axes keep their source animation and receive no keys on the new layer. The choice applies to every loaded control.

Start / end

The first and last frames to preview and bake. Include time after the driver stops so the swing can settle. A bake layer fades on over the frame before Start and fades off over the frame after End. Extend Maya's playback range if needed.

Save preset

Save the spring settings, output axes, endpoint mode, and bake optimization options to a JSON file. The preset does not store rig control names, frame range, or a custom locator's position.

Load preset

Restore settings from a saved JSON preset. Your rig controls are kept. Check the endpoint and refresh source afterward. Older presets keep their manual axis/length behavior and default to all output axes and an unoptimized bake.

Add to shelf

Choose your preferred Maya shelf, then use File > Add to current shelf. Overlap adds its custom 32 by 32 icon and saves the shelf. Running this again updates the existing Overlap button on that shelf instead of adding another. Keep the tool folder in its installed location.

Spring settings

Stiffness

How quickly the spring follows the original motion. Lower values give slower movement and more lag, which can feel heavier. Higher values follow faster and feel tighter. Hz describes the spring's response rate; it is not a mass setting. Try 1.5 Hz for a restrained pendulum.

Damping ratio

How quickly the swing loses energy. Lower values keep it bouncing longer; raising it toward 1 suppresses bouncing. Values above 1 can return to rest more slowly, with little oscillation. Try 0.35 for a longer swing with some bounce, or 0.5 for quicker settling. Very low damping can produce large swings.

Effect strength

Blend between the original motion and the simulated overlap. 0 keeps the original motion; 1 uses the full effect. Lower this if the swing is too large. A value such as 0.65 gives a more restrained effect without changing the spring settings.

Minimum substeps

The minimum number of small simulation steps taken inside each frame. More steps improve accuracy during fast movement but take longer to calculate. This controls simulation quality, not weight or bake key spacing. 16 is a useful starting point; the solver may use more automatically.

Preroll frames

Evaluate this many frames before Start to prepare the spring's initial state. Those extra frames are not baked. It uses the existing animation before Start; it does not invent extra movement. 12 is a useful starting point.

Slower motion: lower stiffness a little. Longer settling: lower damping a little. Smaller swing: lower strength. Change one value at a time. These controls shape the appearance of weight; there is no physical mass control.

Endpoint and direction

Fallback tip length

The distance from the final control's rotation pivot to its virtual endpoint, measured in scene units. It is used in Manual mode, or when Auto has no preceding selected segment. It helps define the lever for rotation. Auto chain placement or a custom endpoint overrides it.

Endpoint direction

Auto continues the previous chain segment beyond the final pivot, so a hanging chain gets an endpoint below its last control. Manual uses the fallback axis and length instead. A custom locator takes priority. After changing this, replace an existing endpoint locator and refresh source.

Fallback tip axis

The local direction used for a manual endpoint, such as -Y for a downward segment. This is the segment's direction, not the channel you want to rotate. A Rotate X hinge needs its endpoint off the X axis. Auto chain placement or a custom locator overrides this setting.

Create / replace endpoint

Create a movable locator for the final segment, or replace this session's existing locator using the current direction settings. Place it toward the end of the hanging part, beyond the last pivot. Do not reload the selection with this locator selected. Refresh source after moving it.

The virtual endpoint supplies a lever for rotation. A downward segment swinging about X needs a tip away from the X axis. A tip placed on the rotation axis cannot produce useful swing around that axis. After changing endpoint direction settings, replace an existing locator and refresh source.

Preview, bake, and recreate

Refresh source + preview

Read the current source animation, solve the spring, and build animated locator previews. Use this after editing source keys, parents, frame range, or endpoint placement. To replace a previous pass, mute its bake layer first. The original rig is driven only after Bake.

Update preview from cached source

Reuse the source animation already sampled, then calculate a new preview with your current stiffness, damping, strength, substeps, or output axes. It is faster than sampling again. If you changed source animation or endpoint placement, use Refresh source instead.

Optimize bake

Remove unnecessary output keys while keeping the first/last keys and sampled swing peaks. The simulation stays at full quality. With this off, every frame is keyed. With it on, the tolerance controls how closely the reduced curves follow the full bake.

Bake tolerance

The maximum allowed difference per baked channel when optimization is on. Rotation uses degrees; translation uses scene distance units. Lower values retain more keys; higher values permit fewer. Start at 0.25 degrees. This is a channel error limit, not the total world-space error at the end of a chain.

Bake to new animation layer

Apply the previewed motion to the actual controls on a new override animation layer. Only checked channels are keyed; original source curves remain. Mute the layer to compare. Optimization settings can change after preview. Undo removes a successful bake; refresh source before another pass.

Delete bake

Choose a generated bake layer from the Bake layer list, then click Delete bake. This removes that layer and its baked curves, preserving original source keys and the rig. Saved bake layers can be selected after reopening a scene. Maya Undo restores a deleted layer. Refresh source before creating a replacement pass.

Clear session helpers

Remove this window's preview locators and endpoint, and discard its cached source and simulation. The loaded control list and settings stay. Baked animation layers and the rig remain in the scene.

Optimization measures error per local channel. Rotation tolerance is always degrees; translation uses scene distance units. A smaller tolerance keeps more keys. The simulation and cached preview keep their full resolution. Reduced curves retain linear tangents, sampled peaks, and the first and last keys.

The layer has full weight inside the frame range and zero weight outside it, with one-frame linear transition handles. Disabled channels and original animation curves remain untouched.

Suggested numbers and examples

These are starting points, not universal presets. Source speed, segment length, and the rig change the result. The restrained pendulum row is the approved example tested during development.

FeelStiffness (Hz)DampingStrengthSubsteps
Restrained pendulum1.500.350.6516
Tighter follow2.000.500.6516
Small secondary accents2.500.600.3516
Slightly longer settling1.500.280.5516

Pendulum example

Load top, middle, and end controls; keep the animated parent out of the simulation list. Choose Rotation, X only if X is the bend axis. Use Auto endpoint direction, 12 preroll frames, and a range such as 1–240 to include settling. Start with the restrained pendulum row.

Optimized bake example

ToleranceUse
0.10°Closer matching; usually more keys
0.25°Useful starting point for a reduced rotation bake
0.50°Fewer keys with a larger allowed difference

The approved 240-frame, three-control pendulum test reduced 720 keys to 184 at 0.25° tolerance. Results vary with the motion. For translation, try a tolerance such as 0.01 scene units and inspect it.

Troubleshooting

  • Nothing swings: check the source has movement and all intended controls are loaded.
  • Preview locators move but the mesh does not: click Bake to apply the result to the controls.
  • The last control does not swing in the intended plane: use Auto endpoint direction and replace the locator.
  • Too much motion: reduce strength first, then raise damping slightly.
  • The swing stops too soon: extend the frame range and lower damping a little.
  • A replacement pass looks exaggerated: check whether previous output layers were left active during source sampling.
  • Unsupported transform/channel: use unlocked, keyable FK transform controls on enabled axes. Unit scale, no shear, and zero rotate axis are required. Offset pivots are supported; do not reset rig pivots.
  • Delete bake is disabled: no generated output layers were found. Create a bake first or reopen a scene containing one.
